response.sql: WITH name_stats AS (SELECT r.name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM name_stats), kept AS (SELECT n.* FROM name_stats n, overall o WHERE n.cnt > o.avg_cnt) SELECT AVG(k.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(k.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(k.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_count FROM kept k, overall o;

assumptions.assumption: Race names are grouped as-is, so same-named races from different seasons are pooled into one group.
The inner JOIN to races drops driverStandings rows whose raceId has no match, as the request specifies.
AVG(ds.points) ignores NULL points, while COUNT(*) counts every joined driver standings record regardless of whether points is NULL.
The overall average count is the unweighted mean of the per-race-name counts, one value per race name, as the request states.
